ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $O$ is a point inside the equilateral triangle $ABC$, with $\angle BOC = 150^\circ$. Triangle $BOC$ is rotated counterclockwise around point $C$ to obtain triangle $ADC$. Connect $OD$ and $OA$. What is the degree measure of $\angle ODC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the property of rotation, we have $CD=CO$, $\angle ACD=\angle BCO$,\\
since $\angle ACB=60^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle DCO=60^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\triangle OCD$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus $\angle ODC=\boxed{60^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right; point O is located inside triangle ABC. The figure also marks point D on the right, and connects line segments such as OA, OD, OC, CD, showing the relationship that triangle BOC is rotated about point C to obtain triangle ADC. Triangle ABC is an equilateral triangle. Reasoning: Because triangle BOC is rotated about point C to obtain triangle ADC, the rotation center C remains fixed, point B corresponds to point A, and point O corresponds to point D. Since ABC is an equilateral triangle, ∠BCA = 60°, so the magnitude of the angle of rotation from ray CB to ray CA is 60°. Thus when point O is rotated to point D, CO = CD, and ∠OCD = 60°. In triangle OCD, CO = CD, and the vertex angle ∠OCD = 60°, so the other two base angles are also equal, and each is (180° - 60°)/2 = 60°. Therefore triangle OCD is an equilateral triangle, and ∠ODC = 60°.
